title: bf16/f16 MACC draft contract
boundary: Actual lower_bf16_matmul_f32acc input/output, including its optional lower_model entry invocation.
example:
+0-initialized half matrix product
→ extend operands to f32
→ accumulate in original order
→ truncate once to the original half format
claim: Complete equality to the source-derived draft reference and strict nonempty local-site qualification. Numerical approval remains abstracted; no original-source equivalence claim.
proof:
MerlinVerify.Check.Bf16F32AccBoundary.check_sound
Exact reference + strict sites + complete source denominator
limit: Explicit selection only; excluded from all. Matching bf16 or f16 formats, checked +0 initialization and maps. Mixed source formats and nonzero initialization refuse. Independent policy review is pending.

title: Ordered unrolling
boundary: The actual source loop → the Python producer's unrolled loop, before tensor preprocessing.
example:
Dynamic outer loop stays in place.
Its inner 5 iterations become 2 groups × 2 lanes + 1 tail.
Zero outer trips still execute no inner work.
claim: Equal returned values, modeled errors and terminal world, under the common scalar/SCF interpretation.
limit: Explicit one-based depth; static selected index64 controls, arbitrary supported dynamic ancestors and partial calls. Current selected-depth qualification covers innermost loops. Captured strides in retained deeper bodies remain a safe refusal pending auxiliary projection qualification. Resource limits apply.

title: Ordered tiling
boundary: The actual source loop → ordered one-dimensional segments. Runs alone or after unrolling.
example:
7 groups
→ segments [3, 3, 1]
A short final segment retains the original order.
claim: Scalar route: equal returns, modeled errors and terminal world. Memory route: the whole storage chain's successful-observation relation.
limit: Depth is selected at the actual tiling stage after unrolling. Public inner TILE and combined UNROLL→TILE gates/native controls pass with exact intermediate/output custody. Retained deeper-body captures remain under qualification; private-buffer tiles retain size2–16.

title: Private buffer reuse
boundary: Original → shape-normalized → reused, with an optional fourth actual segmented output.
interface:
Options(buffer_allocator='total_private_unobservable')
--validate-passes buffer_reuse
# Optional tile_size=2 additionally selects initializer segmentation.
example:
Allocate A → initialize → use → free
Allocate B → initialize → use → free
→ reuse one private slot for both lifetimes
claim: Equal sets of possible successful public observations under the explicitly selected total, private, unobservable allocator model.
limit: Static rank-two i8/i16/i32/i64 rectangular initialization, sequential disjoint private lifetimes. Untiled and tiled actual outputs have proof routes. Explicit total/private/unobservable allocator; no finite-capacity, complete failure-state or native allocator proof.

title: Tensor dead-code elimination
boundary: Exact IR immediately before and after the compiler's preprocessing pruning.
claim: Strict tensor-stage refinement on inputs of the declared types, with source support established.
limit: Only modeled effect-free tensor/scalar operations may be erased. Numerical preparation and native lowering are separate boundaries.

title: Q/DQ proposed-model refinement
boundary: Actual xDSL Q/DQ pass, or complete textual preprocessing including its returned output.
example:
Q/DQ source operations
→ specified ordered scalar expansion
An injected multiply-to-add bug stops compilation.
claim: Strict typed refinement under the proposed Q/DQ source semantics. Optional fresh original PT2/source correspondence is reported separately; source-spec approval is false.
limit: Explicit-only proposed source model, outside all. Pinned producer/Torch native source capture has been qualified. Optional proved prefix composes captured IR through final output and reopens foreign sources after composition. Definedness, broader source formats and independent semantic approval remain open.

title: Common-subexpression elimination
boundary: The leading CSE in the build's actual runner, before tensor bufferization.
claim: Strict tensor-stage refinement; operand aliases and captured region values are checked.
limit: The trailing LLVM CSE is not this gate. Unsupported SCF/memory inputs are not silently covered by the tensor checker.

stage: Instruction IR / Kernel · Before command emission
title: Redundant configuration writes
boundary: Original typed ISA/effect selection owns the actual instruction or straight-line Kernel cleanup before the ordinary consumer.
example:
set configuration = (3, 5)
work
set configuration = (3, 5)
work
→ retain the first setter and both work calls
claim: Equal modeled defined-entry observations, successful state and complete error/terminal state, under one admitted instruction interpretation.
limit: Explicit selected ISA/effect interpretation, outside all. Constant pure setters, complete actual entries and failure states. Nested instruction regions need another context bridge. Implementation/frame contracts require independent review.

title: Invariant configuration hoisting
boundary: The public hoist_loop_configuration producer under its original typed ISA/effect selection, before the existing Kernel consumer.
interface:
PassValidation(..., passes=frozenset({'configuration_loop_hoisting'}))
hoist_loop_configuration(kernel, adapter, pass_validation=validation,
  selected_contracts=original_selection)
# Indexed data uses an explicitly selected proposal_adapter.
example:
loop A: set cfg=3; workA(i)
loop B: set cfg=5; workB(j)
→ set3; loop A: workA(i)
   set5; loop B: workB(j)
claim: Complete modeled outcome/error/terminal-state equality under all-index Models, with exact full command contexts, frame/atoms and terminal join for each motion.
limit: V1 static, V2 retained IV data, V3 overlapping setter prefixes, V4 multiple flat positive loops. 90 distinct current-source cases, fresh replay and prior-profile compatibility pass. Current extent admission is at most 1,000,000. Nested commands, completion fields and dynamic configuration values remain unsupported; model/hardware approval stays separate.
